description:
This map displays two side-by-side views of a rural-urban fringe area, illustrating the application of generalization rules for land cover mapping based on Spot 5 satellite imagery (2.5 m resolution, 1/2/3 band combination) from 2011-07-23 (© CNES 2011, Distribution Airbus DS/Spot Image).
The yellow outlines delineate land cover classes: "1110" represents Urban fabric (specifically low urban density areas, equivalent to CORINE Land Cover (CLC) class 1.1.1), and "2110" represents Arable land.

The left map, labeled "Example of non-generalized urban delineation," shows an initial mapping where urban areas (1110) are fragmented, with multiple separate polygons representing individual buildings or small clusters. Black arrows highlight a narrow gap between two urban polygons. A distinct agricultural parcel (2110) is visible, surrounded by other land cover types.

The right map, labeled "Urban area generalized delineation," demonstrates the application of generalization rules. The urban fabric (1110) polygons are now connected and smoothed, with gaps of less than 50 metres closed, and individual urban segments merged to represent the "whole structure" of the low urban density area, including features like private gardens. The agricultural parcel (2110) remains clearly delineated as agricultural land, consistent with mapping guidelines that such parcels contained within urban surroundings should retain their agricultural classification.
